data.name: Muhannad
data.long_meaning: One who is given a pledge or covenant. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'ahd' meaning covenant or pledge. Muhannad is a title given to those who have taken a pledge or vow to Allah, and is often used to describe those who have completed the Hajj pilgrimage.

in_arabic.name: مُحَنَّد
in_arabic.long_meaning: مُحَنَّد: اسم علم عربي، مشتق من الحنادة، التي تعني المنعقد، وبالتالي معناه المنعقد، أو المنحمد؛ وفي بعض الأحيان، يعني المنحمد للنبي، وذلك لانجاز المهمة، وتنفيذ الأوامر، وبالتالي، يعبر عن الشخص الذي يتمتع بالقدرة على تنفيذ الأوامر، والمساهمة في تنفيذها، والتحKir من خلاله.

historical_references.reference: Muhammad ibn Abdullah, known as Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyah or Muhannad, was the eldest son of Imam Ali and Fatimah bint Muhammad, the Prophet's daughter. He was born in Medina around 600 CE and was a prominent figure in the early Islamic community, especially in Kufa, Iraq. He is considered a Shia imam and is revered for his scholarly pursuits and piety. Muhannad died in 652 CE during the Battle of Al-Harra, a rebellion against the Umayyad Caliphate.
